answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, the network partitions state verification into an unyielding tundra of zero-knowledge challenge proofs and an oasis of high-trust settlement. When an entity registers multiple synthetic identities within the productive orchard of agents, each additional node demands cryptographic stake burning scaled quadratically: cost C(k) = B * k^2. By imposing superlinear economic friction, exponential capital exhaustion renders swarm attacks unviable.
